correctness.rationale: Commutation with the involutive twist forces a 1+2 block matrix. Combining the exact involution equations with the product-integrability equations forces the upper-right block entry to vanish, leaving only four sign patterns; after excluding plus or minus the identity, exactly the two affine families and plus or minus alpha survive. The perfect identity is checked on the generating nonzero basis bracket. The automorphism group and conjugation action are derived directly from bracket preservation. Exhaustive checks over three odd prime fields reproduce the classification, perfect sublocus, and four orbits.

value.rationale: The source presents this example specifically to illustrate product structures, making its complete operator locus a natural structural question. The answer is concise but nontrivial: two affine families coexist with two isolated perfect structures, while the full automorphism quotient collapses to exactly four classes over every field of characteristic not two. This clarifies which structures are genuinely distinct and supplies exact finite-field moduli.
